INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE June 10, 2020 PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY MEETING

The Public Financing Authority meeting for La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Finaning District
will be closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize
the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via
teleconference with all Authority members participating remotely. Considering this, the
customary meeting format has been modified. Even with this change in format, the City is still
encouraging public participation and wishes to make residents aware of the following
opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Send an email in advance if you wish to make a comment on a specific agenda item.
  Please submit your comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. We ask that you
  provide those emails before 8:00 a.m. on June 10th so that staff will be prepared to read
  them aloud at the appropriate time during the meeting.

  3) If you wish to make a comment during the meeting, we will be monitoring the above
  email address and will make every effort to include your comment into the records.
  Please be aware there is a delay in the live stream service and any comments should be
  submitted as soon as possible.

  4) For individuals that wish to share their comments directly during the live stream, you
  may email the planning@cityoflaverne.org by 8:00 a.m. on June 10th with a phone
  number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate
  time during the meeting for your comment.
   CITY OF LA VERNE

  PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  AGENDA

  Wednesday, June 10, 2020, 9:00 a.m.
  Watch Live at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750

Attendance and participation at the Public Financing Authority meetings are welcomed and
appreciated. As a result of the current stay-at-home orders, participation is limited to viewing the
meeting online at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream with submittal of public comments to
planning@cityoflaverne.org up to and during the public hearing. Community engagement
provides the Authority with valuable information. In compliance with the American Disabilities
Act, any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to
participate in a meeting should contact the Assistant City Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at
least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

  Staff Recommendation:  Per State Law, the Authority Board should open the public

  and then take action to modify or reject the IFP pursuant
  to Government Code Section 53398.66
 4.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is the time set aside for anyone
  wishing to address the La Verne Financing Authority on items not listed in any other place
  on the agenda. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the legislative body is prohibited
  from talking or engaging in discussion on any item not appearing on the posted agenda.
  However, your concerns may be referred to staff or set for discussion at a later date. Any
  person desiring to speak will need to email their comments to planning@cityoflaverne.org
  prior to the close of the public comment period. Please include your name and address for
  the record. The Chair reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments.

5.  ADJOURNMENT – The next meeting of the Public Financing Authority will be on July 29,
  2020 at 9:00 AM and is expected to be streamed on the city’s website
  www.cityoflaverne.org/stream but may be held in person at City Hall, 3660 D Street, La
  Verne, California 91750 should state and county orders allow for public gatherings at that
  time.

CITY OF LA VERNE
City Manager's Office
DATE:  June 10,2020

TO:  Public Financing Authority

FROM:  Bob Russi, City

SUBJECT: Second Public Hearing on the draft Amended and Restated lnfrastructure Financing
  Plan for the Enhanced lnfrastructure Financing District (EIFD)

AGENDA SUMMARY

ln October ot 2017, the City Council and the Public Financing Authority (PFA) approved the
lnfrastructure Financing Plan (lFP) for the Enhanced lnfrastructure Financing District (EIFD) and
allocated the property tax increment for the District. Since then, Los Angeles County has agreed to
participate in the District. ln order to accommodate the County, the PFA directed staff to prepare an
amendment to the IFP which would include the County's participation. This draft IFP has been
approved by the County and the City and has been distributed to all property owners and taxing
agencies in the District. Per state law, three (3) public hearings shall be held prior to the PFA
adopting the lFP.

RECOMMENDATION

For this second public meeting, per state law, the PFA is recommended to hold a public hearing,
taking any additional public comment (or any that has been received), and then take action to modify
or reject the lFP. lf the IFP is not rejected, then a public protest hearing would be held on July 29,
2020 al9:00 am.

BACKGROUND

After the City formed the Public Financing Authority (PFA) and approved the lnfrastructure Financing
Plan (lFP) for the Enhanced infrastructure Financing District (EIFD), staff continued discussions with
Los Angeles County (County) on their participation in the EIFD. The County subsequently adopted a
policy that identified the requirements for their participation'

Staff presented the concept of joining the EIFD to the County's Economic Development Committee,
who eventually agreed with the proposal for the County to contribute 50% of their property tax
increment to La Verne's EIFD. The Board of Supervisors voted to participate in La Verne's EIFD in
January of 2020.

The financial information in the IFP needed to be updated to accurately reflect the City contributing
1OO% of its property tax increment and the County's 50% contribution. The amended IFP attached to
this report rbftects ihat change, and other references to the County's participation. ln addition, with
the County becoming an affeLted taxing entity, per EIFD law, they now must have a seat on the PFA.
Previously the PFA was made up of former Mayor Pro-tem Rosales, current M3Yor Hepb_urn and
current M-ayor Pro Tem Carder, and two members of the public (Gilbert lvey and Raymond Skelton).
With the County's participation, one of the three Councilmembers needed to be replaced by
Supervisor Kathiyn Barger. Ultimately, after former Mayor Pro Tem Rosales' retirement from the
Council, Mayor Hepburn and Mayor Pro Tem Carder represent the City of the PFA.
 Per state law, three public hearings before the PFA need to be held before the PFA can take action
on the IFP as prepared. The PFA held a public hearing on May 6, 2020 to accept any public
testimony, of which there was none. The purpose of this hearing is to determine if the IFP should be
rejected outright, modified, or to continue as drafted to the protest hearing which is anticipated to be
held on July 29,2020.

The draft IFP was provided to all property owners and a public workshop was held on Febtuary 27,
2020, where only one property owner attended. However, an initial workshop on the EIFD was held
in March of 2016 where several owners attended and did not express any concerns wlth the concept
of the EIFD.

ln response to the elimination of redevelopment agencies the State legislature approved SB 628
which created an easier path for the creation of tax increment financing for the purpose of funding
public improvements referred to as Enhanced lnfrastructure Financing Diskict (EIFD). EIFD's
provide an opportunity for agencies to issue bonds for an array of public projects as well as support
economic development efforts in specific areas. Those areas of particular interest to La Verne are
connected to improving sustainability and transportation oriented development projects.

Considering the areas that EIFD's can serve, the City Council requested staff to evaluate whether an
EIFD could be used to facilitate development adjacent to the future Gold Line station and complete
the public improvements to help fulfill critical elements of the City's OTLVSP that was adopted by the
City Council in March of 2013.

To that end, numerous steps have been taken to assess the benefits of this approach. These have
included hiring a consultant to evaluate different options for funding necessary improvements,
understanding the financial pros and cons of increment financing, identifying p@ects to be funded
through the EIFD, working in partnership with major stakeholders (ULv/Fairplex), meeting with
property owners of the proposed district to gage their support, and engaging the County on their
possible participation in the District.

The IFP is the document that specifically defines the boundaries of the EIFD, identifies the proposed
projects, and provides the financial analysis of expected tax increment over the life of the EIFD to
allow for the issuance of bonds to pay for the listed improvements. As a summary:

Goals of District - Overarching purpose of La Verne's District is to fund the improvements necessary
to accommodate Transit Oriented Development (TOD) in the corridor of the Gold Line rail system.
This effort will be achieved in three specific areas: lmprovements to aesthetics; enhancement of
connectivity; and expansion of existing utilities.

District Boundaries - The Diskict will be comprised of 83 parcels covering approximately 142 acres in
three separate subareas. These subareas generally encompass First Street to the southern city
Boundary from White Avenue to Fairplex Drive/E Street and undeveloped land west of Wheeler East
of Flood Channel from Puddingstone Drive to Arrow Highway.

  - lt is proposed that 14 projects at an estimated cost of $33 million will be
funded by the district. The improvements are geared toward fulfilling the goals of the d istrict.
Examples include: Street and traffic improvements, pedestrian connectivity, and utility improvements'
